title: Salaried Individuals — Returns, Forms and Tax Slabs for AY 2026-27
publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
supports: Tax slabs, surcharge bands, s.87A rebate limits, marginal relief bands, Chapter VI-A deduction limits and ITR-form eligibility conditions for AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26). Page states last updated 09-Jul-2026.
note: Official Income Tax Department guidance page. Slabs and rebate limits cross-checked against the Finance Act 2025 amendments to s.115BAC.

title: The Income-tax Act, 1961 (as amended)
publisher: India Code / Ministry of Law and Justice
supports: Statutory basis for all provisions cited for FY 2025-26 and earlier, including s.111A, s.112, s.112A, s.50AA, s.56(2)(x), s.80C, s.87A, s.194A, s.194BA, s.234A–234C.
note: Canonical repository. Section text should be re-verified for each specific proviso at review time; the searchable India Code entry is the authoritative copy.

title: The Income-tax Act, 2025 (effective 1 April 2026) and the 1961↔2025 section mapping utility
publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
supports: Statutory basis for Tax Year 2026-27 onwards: 536 sections across 23 chapters, single 'tax year' concept replacing previous year/assessment year, new-regime provisions consolidated in s.202, TDS consolidated in s.393, rebate in s.156, and renamed forms (Form 16→130, 26AS→168, 15G/15H→121).
note: The Act 2025 is a reorganisation rather than a rate change: slabs, capital-gains framework and deduction limits continue, largely with renumbered sections. Arthanomy publishes both the 1961 references (for AY 2026-27) and the 2025 references (for Tax Year 2026-27) and flags the mapping as provisional until each provision is individually confirmed.

title: Reserve Bank of India — notifications, master directions and statistical releases
supports: Monetary policy, deposit insurance limits under the DICGC Act, NBFC and NBFC-P2P regulatory framework, master directions on lending, KYC, and the Bank Rate / repo-linked benchmark regime for floating-rate retail loans.
note: Landing page. Individual master directions and circulars are cited by title in articles and must be re-verified against the RBI website at each review because RBI periodically consolidates master directions.

title: RBI Database on Indian Economy (DBIE)
supports: Macroeconomic time series: CPI/WPI inflation, policy rates, G-sec yields, credit growth, household financial savings, exchange rates.
note: Free public access; redistribution of extracts should attribute the RBI as the source.

title: Securities and Exchange Board of India — regulations, circulars and investor disclosures
supports: Mutual fund categorisation (Oct 2017 circular, as amended), REIT and InvIT regulations, AIF regulations, PMS regulations, ESOP and insider-trading regulation, market-conduct rules, and enforcement orders.
note: Landing page. Arthanomy treats SEBI circulars as the binding source and records the circular date in each article; circular titles are cited verbatim rather than paraphrased.

title: SEBI Investor Education and SEBI SCORES grievance-redressal portal
supports: Investor-protection processes, complaint escalation paths, and official statements on unregistered investment schemes.

title: Association of Mutual Funds in India — NAV files, scheme data and investor education
supports: Daily NAV data for all schemes (machine-readable NAV file), monthly AUM and folio statistics, scheme-category definitions and investor-awareness material.
note: AMFI is an industry association, not a regulator. AUM and flow statistics are self-reported by members and should be read as industry data, not audited market aggregates.

title: National Stock Exchange of India — market data, contract specifications and archives
supports: Listed-security trade data (bhavcopy archives), index methodology and levels, derivative contract specifications and lot sizes, margin and expiry calendars, and index-constituent composition.
note: Bulk historical data is available through published archives; automated access is subject to NSE's terms of use. Arthanomy uses published archives and does not redistribute licensed real-time feeds.

title: BSE Ltd — listings, corporate announcements and disclosures
supports: Listed-company announcements, corporate actions, shareholding patterns, and historical price series for BSE-listed securities.

title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India — regulations and product filings
supports: Insurance product regulations, linked and non-linked product rules, commission and expense-of-management limits on ULIPs, and insurer financial disclosures.

title: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority — NPS framework and circulars
supports: National Pension System architecture, investment guidelines and asset-allocation caps for NPS tiers, annuity rules, withdrawal and exit conditions, and pension fund NAV data.

title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India — Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code framework and records
supports: Corporate insolvency resolution process mechanics and timelines, resolution-plan statistics, recovery rates, and registered insolvency professional and valuation-agency data.

title: Ministry of Corporate Affairs — company filings and the MCA21 registry
publisher: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
supports: Statutory company filings, charge registrations, director details, annual accounts and the master data used for corporate-entity due diligence.
note: Extracting individual filings is fee-based and subject to MCA terms; factual summaries are used with attribution.

title: RBI Retail Direct — direct participation in government securities
supports: Retail investor access, account-opening conditions and bidding mechanics for dated government securities, Treasury Bills, State Development Loans and Sovereign Gold Bonds in the primary market.

title: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation — CPI, IIP and national accounts
supports: Consumer Price Index series used for real-return deflation, WPI series, and national-accounts aggregates.
note: CPI base years have changed historically (2012 base and the revised series). Arthanomy records the base year alongside any inflation figure it cites.

title: National Payments Corporation of India — UPI and AEPS statistics
supports: Payment-system volumes used when discussing settlement plumbing, mandatory UPI-linked market-payment rails and fraud typologies in retail payments.

title: NSDL and CDSL — depository services, charges and investor disclosures
publisher: National Securities Depository Ltd / Central Depository Services (India) Ltd
supports: Dematerialisation mechanics, ISIN identification, depository charge schedules, pledge and margin-pledge rules, and transmission-on-death procedures.
note: CDSL publishes equivalent information at cdslindia.com; both depositories' fee schedules should be consulted as charges are revised periodically.

title: International Monetary Fund — World Economic Outlook and Article IV consultations
supports: Cross-country growth, inflation and fiscal data; sovereign-risk discussion; global interest-rate context for currency-exposure analysis.

title: Bank for International Settlements — research on credit, leverage and market structure
supports: Empirical research on leverage cycles, bank credit, foreign-exchange settlement, and the statistical properties of asset returns used in risk discussion.

title: OECD — data, working papers and pension statistics
supports: Comparative retirement-system data, household balance-sheet statistics and pension-fund regulation comparisons.

title: International Organization of Securities Commissions — principles and reports
supports: Cross-border regulatory principles, retail-investor protection benchmarks and market-conduct standards used to frame Indian rules in an international context.

title: World Bank Open Data
supports: Long-run cross-country series (GDP per capita, inflation, remittances) used for context and for sanity-checking magnitudes.
note: Provides open-access data under a permissive licence; attribution required.

title: Income Tax Slabs FY 2025-26 & FY 2026-27 (new and old regime)
supports: Cross-check of new-regime and old-regime slabs, s.87A rebate limits and surcharge bands, and the statement that Budget 2026 did not change slabs for FY 2026-27.
note: Commercial tax-filing platform. Used only to cross-check figures that are also drawn from the official Income Tax Department page; never relied on alone for a tax rate.

title: Capital Gains Tax in India: rates, holding periods, exemptions and set-off
supports: Cross-check of post-Budget-2024 capital-gains framework: s.111A at 20%, s.112A at 12.5% with Rs 1.25 lakh exemption, 12-month and 24-month holding thresholds, s.50AA deemed-short-term treatment for specified mutual funds acquired on or after 1 April 2023, the resident-individual option of 20%-with-indexation for land and buildings acquired before 23 July 2024, and the s.54-series exemption framework.
note: Secondary source. One table on this page states LTCG as 13%, which conflicts with the 12.5% rate stated elsewhere on the same page and with the Act; Arthanomy treats the 13% figure as an error and does not use it. This discrepancy is exactly why primary sources are preferred.

title: Income Tax Act 2025: key changes, chapters, slabs and section mapping
supports: Confirmation that the Income-tax Act, 2025 is effective from 1 April 2026 for Tax Year 2026-27 onwards, replaces previous-year/assessment-year with a single tax year, retains the new regime as default (s.202), consolidates TDS in s.393, and renames forms (16→130, 16A→131, 26AS→168, 15G/15H→121).
note: Secondary but detailed, with links to the Income Tax Department's official mapping utility, which is the primary source Arthanomy links for section mapping.

title: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation — deposit insurance cover
publisher: DICGC (wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI)
supports: The statutory deposit-insurance limit per depositor per bank, the scope of covered deposits (and the exclusion of deposits of certain entities), and claim-settlement mechanics.
note: The cover limit is amended from time to time; the operative limit must be confirmed at each review.

title: The Gazette of India (e-Gazette)
publisher: Department of Publication, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
supports: Publication of Finance Acts, notifications and rules, including the date on which a provision comes into force — the primary evidence for distinguishing announcement dates from effective dates.

title: SEBI intermediaries and market-infrastructure institutions register
supports: Verification that a broker, investment adviser, research analyst, portfolio manager, AIF or depository participant is actually registered with SEBI before dealing with it.
note: Registration status changes; readers are directed to the live SEBI register rather than to any cached list.

title: AMFI daily NAV file (machine-readable)
supports: Scheme-level NAV and scheme-code data for computing rolling returns, drawdowns and category statistics from a reproducible source.
note: Plain-text daily file. It is a convenient official-aggregator source, but it is not a substitute for the scheme's own published NAV history in the Scheme Information Document.

title: National Housing Bank and state RERA portals
publisher: National Housing Bank / State Real Estate Regulatory Authorities
supports: Project registration status, promoter disclosure obligations, carpet-area definitions under RERA, and the statutory remedies available to homebuyers.
note: RERA administration is state-level; the central portal links to each state authority. Whether a project is registered can only be verified on the relevant state portal.

title: National Pension System Trust — scheme architecture and NAVs
supports: NPS scheme structure, asset-class definitions (E, C, G, A), central-record-keeping-agency mechanics, scheme NAVs and expense-loaded returns.

title: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation — EPF rates, forms and procedures
publisher: EPFO, Ministry of Labour and Employment
supports: EPF contribution rates, statutory interest-crediting process, Universal Account Number mechanics, withdrawal and transfer rules, and the EPF pension (EPS) split.

title: Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme — scheme notifications and issue terms
publisher: Reserve Bank of India / Ministry of Finance
supports: Sovereign Gold Bond issuance tranches, issue price, interest rate, redemption terms, and the status of each tranche as open or closed.
note: Arthanomy does not assert that SGBs remain open for subscription. New-tranche issuance and secondary-market availability are separate questions and each must be verified against current RBI releases and exchange listings.

title: NSE circulars and contract specifications for derivatives (including expiry conventions and lot sizes)
supports: Contract specifications, strike intervals, lot sizes, expiry-day conventions, and settlement mechanics for index and stock derivatives.
note: Expiry-day conventions were revised by SEBI and exchanges; the operative convention must be confirmed against the current exchange circular rather than older articles.

title: SEBI measures to strengthen the index derivatives framework (final measures, 2024)
supports: Increased contract sizes, weekly-expiry rationalisation, upfront collection of option premium, removal of calendar-spread margin benefit and intraday monitoring of position limits for index derivatives.
note: Cited by title because SEBI's circular URLs are revised when documents are re-issued; the policy measures themselves are recorded with the announcement date and the effective dates stated in the circular.

title: RBI Master Direction — Non-Banking Financial Company — Peer to Peer Lending Platform (Reserve Bank) Directions
supports: NBFC-P2P licensing requirements, permitted business model, the prohibition on platforms guaranteeing returns or providing credit enhancement, lender and borrower exposure limits, escrow-account mechanics, and disclosure obligations.
note: Master directions are periodically updated. Arthanomy records the substance of the framework and directs readers to the current version on the RBI website rather than reproducing clause text.

title: RBI Master Direction — Liberalised Remittance Scheme and FEMA (Current Account Transactions) Rules
publisher: Reserve Bank of India / Ministry of Finance
supports: LRS annual remittance limits, permitted and prohibited purposes, reporting through AD banks, and the interaction of LRS with tax-collection-at-source rules.
note: LRS limits and TCS thresholds have been revised repeatedly by successive Finance Acts. Each is recorded with the financial year to which it applies.

title: SEBI circular on categorisation and rationalisation of mutual fund schemes (as amended)
supports: The five-group scheme taxonomy (equity, debt, hybrid, solution-oriented, other), the 41-odd mandated categories, and the portfolio-holding restrictions that define each category.
note: Categories have been amended since the original circular. Category definitions in Arthanomy articles carry the circular date and a review flag.

title: SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations and SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, as amended, including the small and medium REIT amendments
supports: REIT and InvIT structural requirements, minimum asset and unit-holder thresholds, distribution requirements, leverage limits, valuation-frequency rules, and the framework permitting small and medium REITs for fractional ownership of real estate.
note: Arthanomy distinguishes SEBI-regulated REITs and InvITs from private fractional-ownership platforms, which are not equivalent products.

title: SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, as amended
supports: AIF Category I/II/III classification, minimum investment thresholds, investor-count limits, tenure and extension rules, and the framework under which private credit, venture capital and special-situation funds operate in India.

title: SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, as amended
supports: Minimum investment size for discretionary portfolio management services, fee-structure rules, disclosure requirements, and the distinction between PMS and mutual funds.

title: IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations and linked-product rules
supports: ULIP charge caps (premium-allocation, fund-management, policy-administration and discontinuance charges), minimum guaranteed-return requirements for non-linked savings products, and surrender-value rules.

title: Department of Posts / National Savings Institute small-savings scheme rules and current interest rates
publisher: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance / India Post
supports: Eligibility, deposit limits, tenure, interest-rate fixation mechanism and withdrawal rules for PPF, NSC, KVP, SCSS, MIS and Sukanya Samriddhi.
note: Small-savings rates are administratively reset each quarter. Published rates change; any rate quoted in Arthanomy is stamped with the quarter to which it applies and is not presented as a forward-looking rate.

title: SEBI investor alerts on unregistered advisors, guaranteed-return schemes and unauthorised collective investment schemes
supports: Official red-flag lists, unauthorised-entity alerts and the enforcement route for reporting suspected unregistered schemes.

title: Credit Information Bureau (India) Ltd — credit reporting and free annual report
supports: Credit-report structure, score-band interpretation and the statutory free-report entitlement that borrowers can use to verify how a lender has recorded them.
note: For-profit credit bureau. Its score bands and default-probability mappings are commercial products, not regulated public statistics, and are described as such.

title: Udyam registration and MSME classification thresholds
publisher: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India
supports: Investment and turnover thresholds that define micro, small and medium enterprises, relevant to SME-listing, MSME credit and business-acquisition analysis.

title: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment and timber-yield research
publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
supports: Forest-area statistics, plantation-yield ranges, and international context for agroforestry and timber-rotation claims.

title: ICAR and state agricultural university publications on crop economics and agroforestry
publisher: Indian Council of Agricultural Research and affiliated universities
supports: Crop-yield ranges, cost-of-cultivation studies, plantation rotation guidance for species such as teak, bamboo and sandalwood, and agroforestry model economics.
note: Trial-station yields are research maxima under controlled conditions. Arthanomy presents them alongside farm-gate realisations and failure rates rather than as forecasts.

title: SEBI (REIT) amendment permitting small and medium REITs for fractional ownership of real estate
supports: The minimum asset size, minimum-unit-holder and scheme-registration conditions under which fractional real-estate ownership can be offered as a SEBI-regulated SM REIT rather than as a private contractual arrangement.
note: This is the key distinction between a regulated fractional-ownership product and an unregulated one; Arthanomy applies it as a classification test, not as an endorsement of any platform.

title: NSE Indices methodology and index fact sheets
supports: Index-construction rules, selection criteria and rebalancing frequency for Nifty 50, Nifty Midcap 150, Nifty Smallcap 250, sectoral and factor indices used as benchmarks.
note: Benchmark choice is consequential; Arthanomy records the exact index and its construction rules whenever a comparison is made.

title: RBI and scheduled commercial bank published deposit and lending rates
publisher: Reserve Bank of India / individual scheduled commercial banks
supports: Card-rate and deposit-rate statistics, the spread between term-deposit and lending rates, and the benchmark used in floating-rate retail loans.
note: Product-level rates are published by each bank and change without notice. Arthanomy does not display a live deposit-rate table; it teaches the comparison method and directs readers to the bank's own card rates.

title: RBI Handbook of Statistics on the Indian Economy
supports: Long-run series on household financial savings composition, gross domestic savings, bank deposits, and nominal versus real growth in financial assets.
note: Published annually with a lag; the reference year is recorded with every figure.

title: SEBI orders and enforcement actions
supports: Primary evidence for market-manipulation, insider-trading, unregistered-advisory and collective-investment-scheme cases. Used in fraud articles because orders state findings of fact.
note: An order is a finding at a point in time and may be under appeal. Arthanomy states the order date and the appellate status where known, and distinguishes allegations from findings.

title: National Company Law Tribunal and Supreme Court / High Court judgments on insolvency and investor recovery
publisher: National Company Law Tribunal / Supreme Court of India
supports: Judicial treatment of recovery claims, moratorium effects, ranking of creditors and the practical outcome of insolvency proceedings referenced in distressed-debt analysis.
note: Court records are cited by case name and date; readers are directed to the tribunal portal for the operative order.

title: Sharpe, W. F. (1966), 'Mutual Fund Performance', Journal of Business 39(1)
supports: Origin of the reward-to-variability ratio now called the Sharpe ratio, and its original caveats about using it to rank portfolios.

title: Markowitz, H. (1952), 'Portfolio Selection', The Journal of Finance 7(1), 77–91
supports: The mean-variance framework, the distinction between diversifiable and non-diversifiable risk, and the efficient frontier.

title: Merton, R. C. (1973), 'Theory of Rational Option Pricing', Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science 4(1)
publisher: Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science
supports: Continuous-time option pricing, the origin of the Greeks as partial derivatives of the pricing function, and the assumptions under which the model is exact rather than approximate.

title: Black, F. and Scholes, M. (1973), 'The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities', Journal of Political Economy 81(3)
supports: The closed-form European option-pricing formula, its no-arbitrage derivation, and the assumptions (constant volatility, continuous hedging, no transaction costs) that real Indian option markets violate.

title: Fama, E. F. and French, K. R. (1992/1993), cross-sectional tests of the CAPM and the three-factor model
publisher: Journal of Finance / Journal of Financial Economics
supports: Empirical evidence that market beta alone does not explain cross-sectional equity returns, and the size and value factors that motivate factor-investing discussion.

title: Kahneman, D. and Tversky, A. (1979), 'Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk', Econometrica 47(2)
supports: Loss aversion, reference dependence and probability weighting — the mechanisms behind surrender of insurance policies, chasing of past performers and disposal-effect tax behaviour.

title: Shiller, R. J., online data on long-term stock-market returns and the cyclically adjusted price-earnings ratio
supports: Long-horizon real return series and valuation ratios used to frame the difference between short-horizon noise and long-horizon return expectation.

title: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision — credit-risk and securitisation frameworks
supports: Formal definitions of exposure at default (EAD), loss given default (LGD), probability of default (PD) and expected credit loss, which Arthanomy reuses for retail credit modelling.

title: RBI Financial Stability Report
supports: System-level stress indicators, bank asset-quality trends, and macro-financial risk assessments published semi-annually.
note: Biannual publication; each figure used in an article carries the report's reference date.

title: SEBI/Territorial daily TER and portfolio disclosures by mutual funds
supports: Total expense ratios by scheme and plan, monthly portfolio holdings, and the disclosure basis on which direct-versus-regular comparisons are made.
note: Portfolio and TER disclosures are published by each AMC and consolidated by AMFI. Expense ratios are revised within SEBI's permitted band, so a quoted TER is a point-in-time figure.

title: TRAI regulations on SMS and bulk-communication traceability
supports: The mechanism that makes many large-scale SMS and voice phishing campaigns traceable, and the technical reason sender-ID spoofing became harder after 2021—relevant to financial-identity-theft case studies.

title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (with the Information Technology Act, 2000)
publisher: Ministry of Law and Justice / India Code
supports: Criminal provisions that replaced the Indian Penal Code from 1 July 2024, including provisions on cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery and organised crime, used when describing the legal consequences of financial fraud.
note: Many articles and case summaries still cite IPC sections. Arthanomy states both the historical IPC section and the corresponding BNS provision where the correspondence is clear, and flags any mapping it has not verified.

title: Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 and rules
supports: The reporting-entity obligations, record-keeping requirements and attachment mechanism that shape how fraud proceeds are traced and recovered.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules
publisher: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
supports: Remedies available to retail investors who were mis-sold a product or misled by a representation, and the district/state/national commission structure.
